narrative_purpose: Make the chapter's key biological claim visible: hydrogen rises from the fermenting gut into the gas cells because the microbes that would normally eat it are absent.
subject: A cutaway of a fermentation chamber at the base of a large creature. In the lower part, dark folded gut tissue with a mass of partly digested prey. From it, dense strings of small pale bubbles rise upward through a narrow channel and into a large pale gas compartment above, which is visibly filling. Along the walls of the narrow channel, a thin layer of small rounded microbial cells is depicted as sparse, faded and dying, so the rising bubbles pass them untouched.
scene: A clean warm-toned interior cross-section, dark organic tissue below and the pale luminous gas space above.
camera: Side cross-section view, looking into the chamber, bubbles travelling from bottom to top of frame.
light: Warm amber glow low in the fermenting tissue, cooling to pale cyan luminosity in the gas compartment above; the sparse microbial layer unlit and dim.
palette: Amber and deep brown-indigo in the gut tissue, pale cyan bubbles and gas space, the faded microbial layer in desaturated grey.
style: Painterly naturalist cutaway plate, biological and wet, not schematic.
detail_level: Crisp on the bubble strings and the sparse microbial layer they pass; the surrounding tissue softly textured.
composition: Gut tissue across the lower third, rising bubble channel through the centre, gas compartment across the upper third, plain dark margin on one side for later callout labels.
consistency_notes: The teaching point is that the rising gas passes the microbial layer UNCONSUMED - so that layer must read as sparse and faded, not dense and thriving. No chemical notation of any kind.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no chemical formulae, no molecular diagrams, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style
